name: Ultra, burgundy (1979)
description: Braniff International's 'Ultra' scheme (1978, the colors chosen with Halston) in burgundy, as worn by 727-200s and DC-8-62s in 1979: the body, fin, rudder, tailplane, center engine fairing and nacelles burgundy, with a silver-gray belly. Along the belly's edge two pinstripes, a thin ochre line over a broader light brown-gold one, level along the cabin about 1.1 m below the centerline, then following the belly up the tail cone and on up the fin's trailing edge to the tailplane; the same pair runs up the fin's leading edge, set just inside it. Bands of the two pinstripe colors ring the nacelles and the center engine's inlet just behind their polished lips. 'Braniff' in a heavy, forward-leaning roman with long serifs and a swash, capital B and lowercase, in a light accent color over the forward windows just behind the forward door. No fin mark. Gray wings.

sources.title: Yesterday's Airlines: The Elegance Campaign, Braniff's Ultra Look
sources.note: Evidence only: Ultra unveiled 17 July 1978; eight darker colors (terra cotta, Perseus green, Mercury blue, metallic blue, light Corvette blue, chocolate brown, burgundy, sparkling burgundy); the 25 727s delivered from April 1978 in Ultra, only 12 older 727s repainted; all but two DC-8-62s repainted; the 747s in an orange version with a solid orange belly, except N601BN; a mix of Ultra and Flying Colors to the end in 1982.

sources.title: Yesterday's Airlines: Flying Colors, Braniff's 727-227 Advanceds

sources.title: The Airliner Modeling Site forum: 'Ultra-era' memories (Braniff)
sources.note: Evidence only: colors per airframe from members' memories and slides (N426BN metallic blue and N404BN sparkling burgundy from about 1978; DC-8s N1809E chocolate, N1807 burgundy, N802BN Mercury blue, N801BN and N1806 Corvette blue, N1805 terra cotta, N1803 and N1804 Perseus green; N412BN terra cotta in 1979) and the planned pinstripe pairs.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Braniff International Airways
sources.note: Evidence only: the fleet (115 aircraft in December 1979; 747-200Bs from 1978, 747SPs from 1979, ten DC-8-62s, 79 727-200s over the years), the Ultra colors with Halston and Harper and George, 'INTERNATIONAL' dropped from the 727s' and DC-8s' Ultra titles but kept on the 747s, Calder's painted aircraft.

titles.style: Braniff's Ultra lettering: a heavy, forward-leaning roman with long flared serifs, a capital B with a swash running back under its foot and the rest lowercase, the double f's tall; over the forward windows from about 2 m behind the forward door.

notes: Measured 2026-11-24 for ghost flights. Read on N468BN (October 1980), taken here as burgundy: it's darker and browner than the terra cotta jets on the same day's slides, but no source names its color. Burgundy: DC-8-62 N1807 (1981); 727s not identified for certain (N468BN is a guess). The eight Ultra colors share one drawing (BI1928/ultra-*, differing only in palette, finish, id, name and notes): when one's drawing changes, change them all. Measured on N455BN (fitted within 6 px, about 19 px a meter): the thin line's top 1.13 m below the centerline, level along the cabin (within 0.08 m from 3.8 to 29.5 m), the broad stripe 0.22 m deep under it after a 0.07 m gap, the silver below 1.52 m down. Aft of about 32 m the stripes follow the belly's own outline 0.42 m above it (within 0.06 m at 34.8, 37.5 and 38.8 m) up the tail cone, then turn up toward the fin's trailing edge (0.19 m up at 39.4 m, 1.55 m at 40.3 m): that's the outline's curve, not a camera's. The fin's two pairs run 0.02-0.095 of the chord in from each edge; the broad stripe is the outer one on all three edges. The nacelles' bands (three broad, two thin) lie 1.0-2.5 m behind the lip; the same bands round the center engine's S-duct inlet aren't drawn: the fin's space carried down over the fairing runs straight down from the root and out past the leading edge, so there's no way to place them. The title's capital B is about 0.85 m tall, its foot about 0.15 m over the windows' tops, from 7.3 to 12.0 m back (N455BN). It leans forward on both sides. Registrations (small, in the title's color, aft of the wing) and the nose-gear doors' numbers aren't drawn. The pinstripe pairs follow the photos where they show them and the 1978 plan for each color otherwise (forum memories, evidence only). Colors are read off slides and are approximate. On the DC-8-62 (no DC-8 shape yet) the layout is the same: body color, silver belly with the pinstripes, 'Braniff' forward; drawn here on the 727, it lands approximately.
